introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2019. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Layout of the paper: Section A, Map Work (question 1, the only question of its section); Section B, Physical Geography (questions 2 and 3); Section C, Human Geography (questions 4 and 5); Section D, Cameroon Geography (questions 6 and 7).

Carte non fournie : la question 7(a) s'appuie sur la carte muette du Cameroun remise le jour de l'épreuve (absente du PDF) ; l'énoncé porte « [outline map of Cameroon supplied on the day, not reproduced here] » et le corrigé donne les noms et la position des éléments.

Question 7(c) : le projet de Memve'ele sur le Ntem est cité comme exemple ; l'état de mise en service à la date de la session (juin 2019) n'a pas été vérifié ; les autres rivières citées (Sanaga, Bénoué) sont les exemples sûrs.
Question 7(d) : membres de la CEMAC cités de mémoire (six États) ; à faire relire.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Each feature is shown on the outline map with a dot or a shaded area and a name, and the answers should be listed in a key. Examples:

- **(i) A major soil type**: **volcanic soils** on the slopes of Mount Cameroon (South West Region), which are rich and support plantations. (Or the red ferralitic soils of the southern forest zone.)
- **(ii) A climatic zone**: the **equatorial (Guinean) climate of the south** (the South, Centre, East and Littoral Regions): hot, very wet, with two rainy seasons. (Or the Sudan-type tropical climate of the north.)
- **(iii) An industrial zone**: **Douala** (the Littoral Region), the main industrial zone of Cameroon.
- **(iv) The economic capital**: **Douala** (the Littoral Region, on the Wouri estuary); **the political capital**: **Yaounde** (the Centre Region, inland).

One mark for each correct name and position (six marks in all: soil, climate, industrial zone, two capitals, and the neatness of the map and key).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe THREE impact of agriculture to the economy of Cameroon.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Employment and income**: agriculture employs a large part of the working population, and gives incomes to farmers and workers on the plantations.
2. **Food supply and exports**: it feeds the population (food security) and gives export crops (cocoa, coffee, bananas, cotton, rubber and palm oil), which bring foreign exchange and government revenue.
3. **Raw materials and other sectors**: it supplies raw materials to agro-industries (for example cotton for textiles, oil palm and rubber for processing) and stimulates transport, trade and services.

One mark for each impact, described.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Name THREE rivers and the HEP project that have been developed on them.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| River | Hydro-electric project (HEP) |
|---|---|
| **Sanaga** | **Edea** and **Song Loulou** hydro-electric stations |
| **Benue** | **Lagdo** Dam |
| **Ntem** | **Memve'ele** project |

(Other valid answers: the Lom, with the Lom Pangar dam, a reservoir that regulates the flow of the Sanaga.) One mark for each river with its project.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Give four reasons why Cameroon is a member of CEMAC.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
CEMAC is the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon).

1. **A larger market**: free movement of goods, persons and capital between the member states widens the market for Cameroon's products.
2. **A common currency**: the common currency (the CFA franc) and a common central bank give monetary stability and make trade and payments easier.
3. **Joint projects and infrastructure**: members share costs of roads, railways, energy and transport links, and harmonize their economic policies.
4. **Co-operation and bargaining power**: the countries are neighbours with common problems and history; together they have a stronger voice in negotiating trade and aid, and in keeping peace and security.

One mark for each reason.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) State FOUR factors that account for the growth of any ONE named industrial region in Cameroon.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Named industrial region: Douala (the Littoral Region).**

1. **Port and transport**: the port of Douala on the Wouri estuary, the railway, the roads and the airport link it to the hinterland and the world.
2. **Power supply**: electricity from the hydro-electric stations of the Sanaga (Edea and Song Loulou).
3. **Large market and labour supply**: the biggest city of the country has many consumers and many workers.
4. **Raw materials from the hinterland and capital**: agricultural produce (cocoa, rubber, palm oil, timber) arrives in Douala; banks and investment make it possible to build industries; government policy supports industrial zones.

One mark for each factor, named and explained.
